Thanks for reporting and for the great reproducer @Settis!

@FroMage I wonder if we should be "resetting" the connection [here](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/70078e0a393378e7fbb89a949ff89481d4c6c831/independent-projects/resteasy-reactive/server/runtime/src/main/java/org/jboss/resteasy/reactive/server/handlers/PublisherResponseHandler.java#L244-L253). I believe it's the right thing to do, but it's a breaking change for sure. WDYT?

In the first case of the conditional you mean? When the head is already written? It doesn't look like we're resetting it here, we just log an error. I do wonder what happens _after_ that. We just close the connection?
Exactly, we close the connection normally, which means that an HTTP client has no way of distinguishing between a normal completion and an erroneous one.

But… how do you close a connection "not normally" then? It's too late to send an error, and since it's streaming, there's no size that the caller expects to at the very least measure that it did not obtain enough bytes.
You asked for it:) The first request shows what happens when the server calls `reset`, the second when it doesn't

I'm sorry, I did not see any method called `reset` in the code you showed. I don't see it in `PublisherReponseHandler`, and I cannot see anything else than `end()` that's applicable in `ServerHttpResponse`. I suppose you're talking about https://vertx.io/docs/apidocs/io/vertx/core/http/HttpServerResponse.html#reset() and perhaps making this accessible in `ServerHttpResponse`?

This screenshot does not help because it does not show the HTTP exchanges.

What I'm curious about is that we have two modes for streaming, essentially:

- Regular streaming, not chunked, and we should push bytes as they are available, and the client has no idea when the data is supposed to end, so if we end the connection, it thinks it's complete, even when we had an error.
- Chunked streaming, where we announce before each chunk how much data will be in that chunk, so if we end the connection before the chunk is completely sent, the client can see that something's missing. But if we have an exception between chunks (or say when we're trying to serialise an object into the next chunk) and we end the connection, the client was not expecting any chunk so it thinks it's complete and cannot know we had an error.

So, IMO while streaming, the client can only realise the connection was closed prematurely in a very specific case of the error closing in the middle of writing a chunk, which is not very helpful.

Apparently, HTTP/2 has an error frame, so we can signal the client.

For HTTP/1, Vert.x says:

> for HTTP/1.x, close the connection when the current response has not yet been sent

Which is not going to help us if we're not in the middle of sending something.
HTTP/1 supports trailers in chunked encoding, let me read up on that.
